_why: THE NEXT 2+1 — the anchor-slide book made MORE PUNISHING by ONE lever: B 1.5 -> 1.6 (input value x1.6^era in place of 1.5^era). Everything else is byte-identical to probe-anch-costslide: the same eight-industry e1 anchor slide, --anchor-cost, in0 1.2, A 2.2, C 1.9, the same ai_value ladder, defines and 24-month bar. The only economic field that moves is the input quantity on the rungs above e0; target_be and wage_pct also differ because the book is generated on the measured-wage basis of 2026-09-20, but neither is emitted as economics (target_be is the building NAME, wage_pct is model-only).
_what_it_is_for: probe-anch-costslide is OUT on one broken run: GBR in CAPITAL ABUNDANCE in run 2 (U* under 5% for six consecutive years 1931-1936 at a mean hoard of 2.46 of its own GDP), with run 1 missing the identical line by one year. F135's mechanism says the pool's INFLOW is our margins, which run at twice vanilla's. B is the lever that cuts every margin above e0 without touching output, and it raises raw-goods demand at the same time, which is where F128 measured the labour going. Both directions attack the break: less inflow -> a smaller hoard; more extraction jobs -> less of the developed world's labour drained into the frontier.
_measured_at_base_prices: ladder_options at GBR@1905, main method only (a design coordinate, NOT a prediction - BALANCE_FRAMEWORK 10.86.2): the median profit% by era goes 1 / 62 / 148 / 284 -> 1 / 53 / 121 / 224. F97's death test is UNCHANGED at 16/17 industries, and capital per unit of output is untouched, which is what makes this a margin lever and not a capital one. Paper, which the user singled out, goes 4 / 72 / 168 / 329 -> 4 / 64 / 143 / 266.
_what_it_will_NOT_fix: Paper stays about 20pp above the median at every rung. That is arithmetic, not an oversight: a uniform ladder multiplies each industry's OWN era-0 margin, so an industry that starts fat ends fatter, and closing the gap needs a per-industry era-0 lever. The only rule-derived one is the graded penalty (--in0-stage), which gives paper 1.30 against the flat 1.20 - about 8% more input value - and which the generator currently REFUSES to combine with --anchor-for. That is the follow-up, not this batch.

_predictions._basis: THE CRITERIA REGISTER (BALANCE_FRAMEWORK 10.83). Stated before the launch, as the no-ceteris-paribus rule requires; these are DIRECTIONS with magnitudes, and the magnitudes are the weak half.
_predictions.world_gdp: 0.85-1.05 (probe-anch-costslide read 0.97 / 1.22). A margin cut lowers GDP; the risk this batch runs is that it lowers it too far - F128's B 1.8 gain-matched STALLED at 0.70, and the lesson there was that a base-price gain match UNDERSTATES the price channel. B 1.6 is deliberately well short of that.
_predictions.pool_H: 2.0-3.0 (was 3.49). The hoard is the largest single block of the loss (poolH 1.38 + worldH 0.87 of 5.50) and the one this batch is aimed at.
_predictions.capital_abundance: the KEY line: NO shortlist member of 50M+ under 5% U* for five consecutive years ending by 1936 at a mean hoard >= 1.5 GDP. probe-anch-costslide broke it in run 2 and missed by one year in run 1.
_predictions.T0: unchanged or slightly better - B does not touch the era-0 rung, whose inputs are x1.2 in both books.
_predictions.PI: 0.80-0.90 (was 0.85). Dearer inputs per unit of output raise building-input demand, which pushes PI UP; if PI goes above 1.0 the lever has overshot.

_stop_rule: THE RUN-LEVEL STOP applies (2+1 batch): a run ending above x1.3 of vanilla's 1936 GDP median is the config's last. Arm stop_watch.mjs at launch - it reads the register's HARD lines, and F151's lesson is to read those BEFORE alignment_check, because one broken run ends the config however well the seeds agree.
_third_run: only on divergence under F114's bands (GDP >= 0.15 apart AND in different bands, or workers >= 0.10 apart AND in different bands).

_branches.hoard_unmoved: B 1.6 + C 2.0 (capital per unit of output 0.64 -> 0.75 at e3), the pool-ABSORPTION lever, which F135 measured as the only one that takes the hoard down while also taking W down.
_branches.stalled_below_0.85: back to B 1.5 and attack the hoard with cost alone.
_branches.paper_still_fat: the graded era-0 penalty combined with the anchor slide - it needs the generator's --anchor-for / --in0-stage conflict lifted first.
